newsitem.title: FRANCE: No recap decision on CNP, state control to stay.
newsitem.headline: No recap decision on CNP, state control to stay.

text.p: No decision has been taken to date concerning a possible recapitalisation of state insurer Caisse Nationale de Prevoyance (CNP), a finance ministry spokeswoman said on Monday.
The spokeswoman also said the group would remain under state control but did not elaborate.
She was responding to a query from Reuters on a report in Le Monde newspaper which said there was agreement in principle on a capital increase of 2-3 billion francs.
The previous centre-right government had envisaged selling a minority stake of around 37 percent of CNP.
The new Socialist-led government's position is still unclear, given that state control does not preclude the sale of a stake.
The state owns 42.5 percent of CNP, while the state-owned bank Caisse des Depots holds 30 percent, La Poste 17.5 percent and the savings bank group Caisses d'Epargne another 10 percent.
Le Monde said the capital increase could be subscribed to "partially or fully" by the Caisse des Depots.
